summary.headline: Coforge Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue $592.2M (up 21.1% QoQ in USD, Encore consolidated for two months) with 16% consolidated EBIT margin, ahead of 15.5% FY27 guidance.
summary.overview: Coforge reported Q1 FY27 with Encore (Encore/In Cora) consolidated from 24 April (revenue from 1 May), lifting headcount by 10,451 to 46,228. Consolidated EBIT margin was 16% and standalone Coforge EBIT was 16.7%, and management says it now expects to exceed the 15.5% consolidated FY27 EBIT guidance. Organic revenue grew 1.2% QoQ in CC, or 5.2% excluding the India government and data center exits; Encore G&A was cut by 40% to a combined 6.6% of revenue. Next-12-month executable order book rose 44.2% YoY to $2.23B, though the $691M quarterly order intake excludes Encore's order flow.

financial_highlights.change: +21.1% QoQ in USD, +33.3% YoY in USD; includes ~2 months of Encore
+5.2% QoQ CC excluding India government and data center exits
Standalone Coforge EBIT margin 16.7%; Encore EBIT margin 20.3% (from call: 20.3% and 19.1% cited)
Encore G&A down 40% from 10% to combined level; Coforge standalone was 6.7%
FCF to PAT conversion 95.3% vs -56.5% in Q1 FY26
vs INR 13.80 in previous quarter; equity base up ~25%

financial_highlights.value: US$10M hedge loss in Q1; US$14M M2M loss to be realised over next two quarters
financial_highlights.change: Expected +US$10M earnings benefit from Q4 onwards
Vs US$15M total integration budget guided at acquisition; US$5.4M in Q4
Organic only; excludes Encore order intake

segments.name: Vertical mix (organic CC QoQ)
segments.commentary: BFS 24.7% of revenue, +2.9% QoQ; Insurance 13.6%, +4.6% QoQ; Travel, transport, hospitality 21.3%, +1.7% QoQ; Healthcare and high tech 17.3%, +11.6% QoQ; Government outside India 6%; Others 17.1%, -8% QoQ after planned exits.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Europe +8.4% QoQ CC and Americas +3.5% QoQ CC; Rest of World -22% QoQ reflecting India government and data center exits. Management says Rest of World margins should expand from here.

segments.name: Service lines
segments.commentary: AI-led engineering 50% of revenue, data services 21%, cloud 15%; AI-led engineering, data and cloud together 86% of revenue, above the 80% indicated at the Encore announcement.

segments.name: Client concentration
segments.commentary: One client above US$100M, three at US$50-100M, 14 at US$20-50M, 29 at US$10-20M; top 5 clients 18% and top 10 clients 26.1% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 20.5% to 21%, unchanged.
FY27 EBIT margin guided at 16.5% to 17% standalone and 15.5% or higher consolidated; management says it now expects to surpass the 15.5% consolidated guidance.
FCF to PAT guided at more than 100% for FY27; Q1 achieved 95.3%.
Q2 expected to be a robust growth quarter; large deals signed in April (including a US$230M five-year European program) to ramp up; most large-deal revenue to start impacting from Q3.
Encore G&A to improve further in Q2 with full-quarter impact of actions; marginal integration cost in Q2 and none from Q3.
Management expects EPS to stay accretive in FY27 despite the acquisition; no broad wage hikes before January next year, with a select group already increased in Q1.
capex_capacity: Headcount 46,228 at end-Q1, net addition 10,451 including 9,256 from Encore; organic net addition 1,195 QoQ.
Utilisation 82.5%, which management is holding deliberately ahead of expected growth; LTM attrition declined to 10.4%.
All 45 Encore legal entities migrated to S/4 HANA effective 1 May.
Term loan of US$550M fully drawn by 30 June; 3-year tenure at 2.99% post-tax cost (4.6% pre-tax, fixed). Repayments: ~US$59M in FY27, US$209M in FY28, US$258M in FY29, US$75M in Q1 FY30.

Acquisition accounting: ~US$480M customer relationship intangibles amortised over 12 years (~US$40M per year); goodwill lower by US$600M after share price at closing was US$20 vs US$18.15 at signing. Management said reported goodwill is INR 120,890M in the filing.
demand_pricing: Order intake US$691M in Q1 from four large deals, organic only; Encore order intake and UK framework agreements are not included and will sit on top.
Management says the industry faces efficiency-driven deflation but cites tailwinds from legacy modernisation, AI-ready data, cloud and security.

Outcome-based contracts are 6-7% of global revenue on a run-rate basis; models include risk-based legacy modernisation, subscription pricing for mod squads, and technology- or business-outcome-linked pricing.
Management said it will not discount price to chase growth, targeting 16% EBIT while aiming to be among the highest-growth and highest-margin mid caps.
Competition: management said Coforge's performance has been materially superior to the industry for nine years, citing domain focus, execution intensity and go-to-market.
Encore: one top-10 client came from the Encore portfolio with a path to US$50M+ over 18 months; two more in the 11-20 client bucket.

qa_highlights.question: How much of order intake is organic versus Encore, and are UK framework agreements included?
qa_highlights.answer: US$691M is organic only and excludes Encore order flow. The UK framework agreements are still outside the reported order intake and will be added on top.

qa_highlights.question: How is the AI monetisation (Neuron, mod squads) reported and what share is TNM vs fixed price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Neuron is an operating layer rather than a platform and cannot give a standalone AI revenue figure; the 86% AI-led engineering, data and cloud share is its proxy. Outcome-based contracts are 6-7% of revenue on a run-rate basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will Encore's G&A rise and what is the cost-out progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined G&A is 6.6% vs Coforge standalone 6.7% and Encore 10%, a 40% cut in Encore G&A. Absolute G&A rose because Encore's headcount was added; the percentage fell.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cloud revenue share fall and is there a reclassification?
qa_highlights.answer: Encore had almost no cloud revenue and was mostly engineering, so engineering share rose about 5% and cloud fell about 2.7-2.8 percentage points. Cloud grew about 4% QoQ in absolute terms.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Rest of World margin not expand after exits?
qa_highlights.answer: The exited India government and data center businesses carried higher margins, and Encore consolidation offset the gain, so margin was flat; management expects Rest of World margin to expand from here.

qa_highlights.question: Ramp-up of the US$158M and US$230M deals and wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: The first deal ramp-up is complete with 300+ FTEs across 15-20 teams, transitioned in under four months. The second deal (US$230M+) has started ramping up with 20-30 teams. Broad wage hikes are not expected before January next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 organic CC growth of 5% QoQ repeatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no hard QoQ guidance; it said Q2 should be robust and that large deals signed in April are already in place.

risks_watch: Encore order intake and revenue growth have not been disclosed separately; management promised more detail next quarter.
Hedge book: US$14M M2M loss over the next two quarters; the hedge impact falls away from Q4.
Deflation from AI-driven efficiency in fixed-price and T&M work; management did not quantify pricing effects.
Integration execution across Encore clients: growth from the top-10 and 11-20 Encore accounts must come through by Q3.
Leverage from the US$550M loan; repayments step up to US$209M in FY28 and US$258M in FY29.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and margins, with management repeatedly claiming an industry-leading position. Evasive on Encore order intake, which was not quantified and is deferred to the next quarter, and on the reconciliation of the goodwill figures.
key_quotes: We believe very strongly that solution led selling. Does not warrant price discounting to accelerate growth.
Excluding one-time exceptional costs, EPS for the quarter was rupees 13.30 compared to rupees 13.80 in the previous quarter.
We are confident of achieving an EBITDA margin of 20.5 to 21% on a consolidated basis.
We remain confident of meeting the free cash flow to PAT guidance of 100% for FY 27.

growth.why: FY27 guidance held (standalone EBIT 16.5-17%, consolidated EBIT at least 15.5%, EBITDA 20.5-21%) with management expecting to beat the consolidated EBIT figure; growth is backed by a US$2.23B next-12-month executable order book (+44% YoY) and US$230M large deal ramping from Q3, but no new capacity is being added and the revenue jump is mostly the Encore acquisition, with organic growth only 1.2% Q

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBIT 16.0% vs 15.5% FY27 guide, management expects to surpass it; hedge loss of US$14M over next two quarters falls away from Q4 (+US$10M benefit) and Encore G&A cut 40% to combined 6.6% with further Q2 improvement.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or sites discussed; headcount rose to 46,228 mainly via Encore acquisition (9,256), with organic net add only 1,195 QoQ, so capacity growth is through acquisition rather than new build.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Organic revenue +1.2% QoQ CC (+5.2% ex India government and data center exits); US$2.23B next-12-month executable order book up 44.2% YoY and US$230M five-year European deal ramping, with most large-deal revenue from Q3 and Q2 called robust.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 82.5%, above the ~80% threshold, but management is holding it deliberately ahead of growth and has not announced any new capex, so a capex call is plausible but not guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says it now expects to exceed the 15.5% consolidated FY27 EBIT guidance after Q1 consolidated EBIT of 16.0% and standalone 16.7%, though standalone 16.5-17% guide was simply held.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: All FY27 guidance (EBITDA 20.5-21%, EBIT 16.5-17% standalone, 15.5%+ consolidated, FCF/PAT >100%) held, with Q1 FCF/PAT at 95.3%; risks are integration and deflation, which were not quantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed; Neuron is described as an operating layer with no standalone revenue figure.

rows.label: Large-deal ramp-up from Q3 (US$230M program)
rows.why: Next-12-month executable order book US$2.23B (+44.2% YoY) with US$691M Q1 organic intake, and the US$230M five-year European program ramping with 20-30 teams, most large-deal revenue from Q3.

rows.label: Encore G&A and integration cost roll-off
rows.why: Encore G&A cut 40% from 10% to a combined 6.6% of revenue, with further Q2 improvement and integration cost of US$6.5M in Q1 (vs US$15M budget) fading to nil from Q3.

rows.label: Wage hikes and deflation pressure
rows.why: No broad wage hikes until January, with a select group already raised in Q1, while management flags AI-driven efficiency deflation in fixed-price and T&M work without quantifying the price effect.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins (now expecting to beat 15.5% consolidated EBIT guide) and the US$2.23B order book, but cautious and evasive on Encore order intake and goodwill reconciliation; analysts pressed on Encore's standalone growth and AI deflation pricing.
